name: Situated evidence fragment
summary: A narrative fragment gains meaning from its author, time, location, condition, audience, and relationship to nearby evidence instead of functioning as detached exposition.
player_action: The player discovers a page, recording, object, message, performance, or resident account and interprets why it exists there.
system_response: The game binds the fragment to a specific source and world context while preserving what remains unknown or disputed.

conflicts_with: fragment claiming events its source could not know

failure_modes: The fragment says the same thing wherever it appears.
The author knows facts unavailable to them.
Collecting the fragment silently converts inference into truth.
The journal strips away the placement that made the fragment meaningful.
accessibility: Provide transcripts, replay, scalable text, speaker identity, and non-audio discovery cues.
Preserve placement and source context in the journal.

smallest_playable_test.setup: One room with four fragments from two sources, one altered object, one deliberate conflict, and a journal that records source and location.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Players reconstruct the bounded event and identify the unresolved conflict without receiving an omniscient summary.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Fragments are understood individually but placement or authorship adds no information.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: A fragment contradicts its available knowledge or the journal asserts a single unsupported account.

evidence.claim: Mobius describes using a translator to decipher ancient writing and environmental tools to investigate mysteries across changing locations.
evidence.notes: Supports fragments whose meaning depends on source, location, and comparison across a world.
